questions.question: Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true even if they do not conform to real-world knowledge, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: 1. All buildings are shops. 2. Some shops are boutiques. 3. No restaurant is a boutique. Conclusions: I. Some boutiques are buildings. II. Some restaurants being buildings is a possibility. III. No restaurant is a shop.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true even if they do not conform to real-world knowledge, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

Statements:

1. All buildings are shops.
2. Some shops are boutiques.
3. No restaurant is a boutique.

Conclusions:

I. Some boutiques are buildings.
II. Some restaurants being buildings is a possibility.
III. No restaurant is a shop.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Least Possible Venn diagrams:

             

Conclusions: 

I. Some boutiques are buildings → Doesn't Follow (As some shops are boutiques and all buildings are shops, so we can not say anything definite about some boutiques are building.it is a possibility)

This possibility scenario can be shown using the below Venn diagram:

Here, No boutique is a building. that is why this statement is a possibility. 

II. Some restaurants being buildings is a possibility → Follow (As no restaurant is a boutique , some boutique are shops and all buildings are shops. so we can not say anything about some restaurants are building, it is a possibility )

This possibility scenario can be shown using the below Venn diagram:

Here, some buildings are restaurants that's why this given possibility is followed.

III. No restaurant is a shop → Doesn't Follow (As some boutiques are shops and no boutique is a restaurant, so Some part of restaurant is not shop, but No restaurant is a shop can be possible only)

Thus, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is " Only conclusion II follows".

questions.question: Direction: In the question below are given four statements followed by four conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts. Statements: Some apple are banana Some papaya are orange All orange are apple Conclusions: I. Some banana are papaya II. Some papaya are not banana III. All apple are orange
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: In the question below are given four statements followed by four conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Statements:

Some apple are banana

Some papaya are orange

All orange are apple

Conclusions:

I. Some banana are papaya

II. Some papaya are not banana

III. All apple are orange

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.html: Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.solution:
Mistake Points

Conclusion (Some + Some not) can never be 'Either or' case.

Complementary pairs for the 'either-or' case are:
1) All + Some not

2) No + Some.

 

Conclusions:

I. Some banana are papaya → False (As Some apple are banana, Some papaya are orange and All orange are apple → No proper relation can be established)

II. Some papaya are not banana → False (As Some apple are banana, Some papaya are orange and All orange are apple → No proper relation can be established)

III. All apple are orange → False (As All orange are apple)

Hence, None follows.

questions.question: Direction: In the question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions numbered I, II and III You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follow

Conclusions:

I. Some Handmade is Metal → False (It is possible but not definite)

II. No Metal is handmade → False (It is possible but not definite)

III. All Steel is Metal → False (It is possible but not definite)

Conclusion I and II form a complementary pair

Thus, only conclusion Either I or II follows.

questions.question: Directions: In the following question, three statements are given followed by three conclusions I, II and III. You have to consider the given statements to be true even, if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and decide which of the following logically follows from the given statements disregarding the commonly known facts. Statements : All Motors are Iron. All Iron are Cheap. Some Cheap are not Products. Conclusion : I. All Products are Iron. II. Some Iron are Motors. III. Some Products are not Iron.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In the following question, three statements are given followed by three conclusions I, II and III. You have to consider the given statements to be true even, if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and decide which of the following logically follows from the given statements disregarding the commonly known facts.

Statements :

All Motors are Iron.

All Iron are Cheap.

Some Cheap are not Products.

Conclusion :

I. All Products are Iron.

II. Some Iron are Motors.

III. Some Products are not Iron.

options.text: Either II or III and I follows
options.html: Either II or III and I follows

options.text: Either I or III and II follows
options.html: Either I or III and II follows

questions.solution:
The logic follows here is :-

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

Conclusion :

I. All Products are Iron → False (No direct relation is given hence, False)

II. Some Iron are Motors → True (All Motors are Iron so, Some Iron are Motors is True)

III. Some Products are not Iron → False (No direct relation given hence, False)

Conclusion I and III are complimentary pairs.

Hence, Conclusions Either I or III and II follows.

Thus, the correct answer is "Either I or III and II follows".

Important Points

Conditions of Either-or case:

1. Individually both the conclusions should be false.

2. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

The two complementary pairs are:

1) All + Some not

2) No + Some

questions.question: In the question below are given three statements followed by two conclusions. You have to take each of the given statements to be true. Read the conclusions and then decide which of the conclusions can be logically derived. Statements: Some schools are colleges. No college is university. All universities are hospitals. Conclusions: I. Some schools are universities. II. At least some hospitals are colleges.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question below are given three statements followed by two conclusions. You have to take each of the given statements to be true. Read the conclusions and then decide which of the conclusions can be logically derived.

Statements:

Some schools are colleges.

No college is university.

All universities are hospitals.

Conclusions:

I. Some schools are universities.

II. At least some hospitals are colleges.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagrams for the given statement is as follows:

Conclusions:

I. Some schools are universities → False (It is possible but not definite).

II. At least some hospitals are colleges → False (It is possible but not definite).

Therefore, it is clear that Neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Neither I nor II".

questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be different from commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: 1. Some cheeses are butters. 2. All oils are butters. 3. No butters are liquid. Conclusions: I. No oils are liquids. II. Some butters are cheeses. III. All butters are oils.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be different from commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

2. All oils are butters.
3. No butters are liquid.

I. No oils are liquids.
II. Some butters are cheeses.
III. All butters are oils.

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Both conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
For this question, the Venn diagram of the statements is shown below-

I) No oils are liquids → Follow → As all oils are butters and no butters are liquids, So we cannot say oils are liquids. 

II) Some butters are cheeses → Follow → As some cheeses are butters. So some butters are cheeses. It is definite true.

III) All Butters are oils → Does not follow → As all oils are butters, So all butters are oils it is not possible.

Hence, the correct answer is "Both conclusions I and II follow".

Some guavas are mangoes.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows :
